title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Booking Status Read at the Issue of Originals
content:
For `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents`, the originals put into circulation when a document is issued depend on whether the cargo has actually gone on board. The test is made on the status of the booking the document covers.

## Rule

1. The cargo is on board for this purpose when the booking stands at loaded, departed or closed.
2. Where the document's type is permitted to issue on a received-for-shipment basis, a booking standing at gated in is treated in the same way.
3. The booking taken into account is the one held under the documentation party's own customer account. If the booking covered by the document is held by somebody else, the line does not read it, and the cargo is taken as not on board.
4. In every other booking status the cargo is not on board for this purpose, and no originals are put into circulation at issue; the number is zero.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Booking status | Received-for-shipment permission on the type | Cargo on board for this purpose? |
|---|---|---|
| Loaded | either | Yes |
| Departed | either | Yes |
| Closed | either | Yes |
| Gated in | Yes | Yes |
| Gated in | No | No |
| Requested, confirmed, equipment released or cancelled | either | No |

## Point of judgement

**A document's booking reference points to a booking under a sister company's separate customer account. Is that booking's loaded status used?** No. Only a booking held by the documentation party itself is read; the other is disregarded and the cargo counts as not on board.
